data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word ‘sweostor’ meaning ‘younger sister’. In Christian tradition, the name Sibby can represent the bond between siblings and the love and support that comes with it. The name Sibby carries the meaning “Little sister” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sibby usually hope their child will grow to embody little sister and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Sibylla
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word sibylle, derived from the Greek word siby, meaning sister. In Latin literature, sibyls were prophetesses who lived in the remote parts of the world and spoke in riddles. The name Sibylla was also used for a legendary prophetess in Roman mythology.

in_english.name: Sibby
in_english.long_meaning: From the English word sibling, which is derived from the Old English word sib, meaning brother or sister.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sibby carries a sweet and innocent charm that can make anyone think of the playful, lovable bond shared between siblings. The name can be given to a baby girl in a family with multiple daughters, signifying the younger sibling and the special role she embraces in her family. Sibby is a name that is deeply rooted in history and tradition, and it continues to be a cherished and meaningful name for many Christian families around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sibby holds a spiritual significance in the Christian faith as it represents the love and unity shared between siblings. As siblings are called to love one another as they love themselves, the name Sibby can serve as a reminder of the importance of familial relationships and the role they play in enriching our spiritual lives. It is a name that embodies the selfless love and support that comes from the bond between siblings and highlights the importance of cherishing these relationships as lifelong treasures.
